A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S-BLACK SWAN framework. All 34 pages of each version, including figures, equations, notation tables and appendices, support comparison despite the changed title and appendix lettering.

before.justification: v2 presents mathematical definitions, proofs, hypothetical examples and discussions of cited evidence. It reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies or empirical data analyses.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical. Its new Appendix B summarizes historical and healthcare examples from cited sources without reporting original empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the distortion functions, and the ground-truth, Human and Human-Estimation MDP framework are retained. Section 5.2's wording changes clarify the existing perceived-trajectory construction.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or benchmarks. Appendix B introduces aerospace and healthcare illustrations, but these domains are not used for training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines. The newly cited healthcare RL work and discussion of Transformers in Appendix B do not constitute experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets or testing procedures are added or revised. The new appendix provides narrative examples without an evaluation design.

E4.justification: Section 4's mathematical cases remain unchanged. Appendix B adds explanatory narratives about cited cases, without new tests or analytical results; no ablation, robustness or sensitivity analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The probability and concentration bounds remain theoretical derivations rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The worked insurance example retains its 1% risk, loss of 1,000 and premium of 15. No measured performance results are added or revised; Appendix B supplies cited illustrations rather than new study outcomes.

T1.justification: v3 inserts the factor (1-gamma^T)/(1-gamma) into Equation (7). Equation (14) is also rebracketed, changing its first weighting term and creating an inconsistency with the expression repeated in Equation (15). The main definitions, assumptions and theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, Hypothesis 1, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same claims about misperception causing black swans in stationary environments. The new title foregrounds human irrationality and AI safety without changing those claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix B interprets Victor Prather's drowning through underestimated operational risk and suggests that inappropriate input selection can obscure hypoglycemia risk. These extend the practical interpretation of misperception beyond the retained examples.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware information, runtime measurements, or code/data access provisions are added or revised. The new supporting examples contain no reproducible experimental procedure.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds Clark (2021), Brinkley (2019), Wang et al. (2023), Panda et al. (2020), and Ambhika et al. (2024). These support the new illustrations; the existing positioning relative to safe RL and cumulative prospect theory is retained.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and publication header, adds acknowledgments and a Supporting Evidence appendix, and shifts existing Appendices B-G to C-H. Local wording, notation and cross-reference edits accompany an otherwise retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2 and the notation table retain their content. Figure 2 moves lower on page 7, some equations are resized, and the added text reflows references and appendices. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B adds practical illustrations, and replacing the broken reference in Theorem 3's proof with Definition 2 improves traceability. Equation (7) also gains an omitted discount prefactor. However, Equation (14)'s new grouping conflicts with the ensuing derivation, and partial g-to-h substitutions in Lemma 1 introduce mapping ambiguity. These localized benefits and regressions leave the net quality direction unclear.
